name: Crucible Industries Sentinel CR-40 'Tombstone'
description:
A heavy conventional sniper rifle chambered in a proprietary 12.7mm round that Crucible designed specifically for maximum terminal effect against cyber-augmented targets. The round carries a micro-EMP charge that detonates on penetration, frying cyberware in a localized radius around the wound channel.

The Tombstone was born from battlefield intelligence suggesting that heavily augmented combatants could survive wounds that would kill an unaugmented human. Crucible's solution was elegant — don't just wound them, kill their augmentations simultaneously. A cyber-limb that goes dead becomes dead weight. A reflex booster that shorts out leaves its user slower than baseline. Ocular implants that fry blind their owner.

The CR-40 is a brutalist weapon — heavy, loud, and unsubtle. It makes no concessions to stealth or portability. It exists for one purpose: to put augmented targets in the ground and make sure their chrome dies with them.
legality: Licensed — military and authorized corporate security
specifications: caliber: 12.7mm EMP-core effective_range: 200-2,000 meters rate_of_fire: Bolt-action, 1 round per 4 seconds capacity: 5-round detachable magazine weight: 14.2 kg power_source: EMP charge is self-contained in each round
tactical_use: The Tombstone is deployed against heavily augmented targets where conventional precision weapons might not achieve a clean kill. The micro-EMP detonation ensures that even a non-fatal hit will disable critical cyberware, leaving the target vulnerable to follow-up engagement. Corporate security teams facing augmented breach teams have adopted the CR-40 as their primary anti-personnel tool, often positioning a Tombstone operator to engage the most heavily modified threat first.
cultural_context: Among the augmented communities of GLMZ, the Tombstone is spoken of with particular dread. A round that kills your chrome is more than a weapon — it is an existential threat to people whose identity is bound up in their modifications. Anti-augmentation extremists have adopted the Tombstone as a symbol, and graffiti of the CR-40's distinctive bull-pup silhouette has appeared in augmented-friendly districts as a threat.
story_hooks: A Tombstone round hit an augmented civilian in a crowded market — the micro-EMP disabled cyberware in everyone within a 5-meter radius. The weapon's designers swore the EMP effect was localized. Something has changed.

An underground augmentation clinic has begun installing EMP-hardened implants specifically to counter the Tombstone threat. Crucible wants to know how they obtained the weapon's EMP frequency specifications.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist sniper rifle with an aggressive, utilitarian stance. The Tombstone presents itself as an industrial tool rather than a precision instrument — all hard angles, pronounced mechanical elements, and uncompromising geometry. Its heavy profile suggests devastating capability over elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 127cm | Barrel length: 71cm | Width (at stock): 8.5cm | Height (with scope): 22cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and substantial — 14.2kg feels present in the shoulder, demanding respect and proper technique. The weight distribution leans forward, anchoring the shooter into a solid firing position.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten-steel composite frame with reinforced polymer furniture. The receiver is machined from solid tungsten-steel billet, while the stock and fore-end utilize military-grade carbon-reinforced polymer.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-black with worn, brushed steel showing through high-friction points. Deliberately austere — no shine, minimal reflection. Scattered micro-abrasions and stress marks suggest field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with dark gunmetal steel accents. Minimal color variation — pure industrial aesthetic with no decorative elements.
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured, hard-molded polymer grip with pronounced finger grooves. The material is gritty, slightly adhesive in feel, designed for retention even in wet conditions or gloved hands.
distinctive_features: Prominent EMP charge indicator window on the magazine housing — a small crystalline component that glows faint amber when armed
Heavy muzzle brake with distinctive trapezoidal vents for EMP payload dispersal
Integrated mounting rail system running full length of top receiver with Picatinny sections
Mechanical safety lever with tactile detents at the rear of the receiver
Charging handle positioned high and rearward, oversized for gloved operation
Magazine well with exposed witness marks indicating round count
Faint electromagnetic shielding patterns etched into the receiver (functional, not decorative)
Serial plate mounted on the left side with Crucible Industries corporate hex logo
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES stamp on the receiver in sans-serif industrial font. Hexagonal Crucible logo below. 'CR-40 TOMBSTONE' designation etched into the barrel shroud. Military licensing marks stamped near the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field weapon — clean mechanicals, properly serviced, but showing evidence of regular deployment. The finish bears the patina of professional military use without being neglected.
